misc: The mathematical and physical relations between these two contributions to non-unitary evolution of the system have been the subject of many studies in quantum relaxation theory over the last 20 years. In the energy eigenbasis dephasing causes decay of off-diagonal elements of the density matrix, while dissipation causes decay of both diagonal and off-diagonal elements. In the context of quantum computation and error correction it has become customary to refer to both types of processes generically as ‘decoherence’. While the original meaning of decoherence was specifically designated to describe loss of coherences in the off-diagonal elements of the density operator in the energy eigenbasis, there are several reasons why one may wish to be less specific for general study of the effects of environmental interactions on quantum information processing. First, there is the undesirable fact that such decay of coherences in the off-diagonal elements of the density operator is basis set dependent. Second, at the physical level, both dissipative and dephasing interactions contribute to this loss of coherence in off-diagonal elements. These two factors render it more preferable in the context of a general consideration of quantum errors to adopt the now common usage of ‘decoherence’ to refer quite generally to loss of unitary evolution and to all underlying physical mechanisms for this

abstracts.value: Decoherence is the phenomenon of non-unitary dynamics that arises as a consequence of coupling between a system and its environment. It has important harmful implications for quantum information processing, and various solutions to the problem have been proposed. Here we provide a detailed a review of the theory of decoherence-free subspaces and subsystems, focusing on their usefulness for preservation of quantum information.
